summary: Skyrise is a spatial auction game where players bid influence to claim hexagonal building sites on a rising modular cityscape, then race to complete neighborhoods, court wealthy patrons, and fulfill objectives before the city tops out. The bidding is the heart of it: you're constantly reading which sites your opponents want and deciding how much of your limited pool to burn to deny or secure them.
praised: clever spatial auction system that's easy to learn but hard to master
strong player interaction through bidding without direct conflict
handsome tactile production with the rising 3D city
good variety from patrons and secret/public objectives
criticised: can suffer analysis paralysis as the bidding board gets crowded
some feel the wonder-building endgame is underdeveloped compared to the main auction
scoring can feel a bit fiddly to track

interaction.detail: Every site is won through a simultaneous or escalating bid against the same pool of rivals, so you are constantly reacting to what others are chasing and can price them out of a site. The city itself is a fully shared board, and neighborhood/wonder scoring depends on who has built where relative to everyone else.

scoring.why: Final score sums several independent categories: completed neighborhood color sets, patron card requirements, public and private objectives, and the shared Wonder bonus.
scoring.how_you_win: You bid spatially to win building sites, construct tiles that satisfy patrons and objectives, and contribute to the Wonder; whoever accumulates the most prestige points across all these categories wins.
